As one sweaty guy to another, here's some advice and learning that may help:

There are two separate issues you're trying to resolve here: Body odor and perspiration. Most "deodorants" available (almost all, actually) are combination "deodorant/antiperspirant". Sweat (perspiration) is generally regarded as the source of body odor, but it actually isn't, the smell is actually caused by bacteria (same reason your jeans smell grungy after three days of wear).

Sweat actually helps clear your pores, so naturally sweating should help avoid causing bad body odor (you might still have a "musky" smell, but there's a big difference between BO and musk). If you sweat so much that it leaks through your shirts, then you may want to address it, but this is better handled with an undershirt than an antiperspirant (if smell is an issue, the antiperspirant would just make it worse).

Another way to understand it is that "deodorant" masks the smell ("putting perfume on a pig", if you will), when what you want to do is prevent it from being made in the first place.

The best thing I've found for this purpose is what's called an "alum block". If my chemical knowledge is failing me here hopefully someone will correct me, but it's essentially a raw piece of a mineral (potassium alum, you might find it online as "potash alum"; I've also seen it branded as "crystal deodorant"). It's an astringent (tightens skin/pores), and inhibits bacterial growth, so the stuff that actually causes the smell can't grow in the first place.

I first learned about it as an aftershave alternative (it's essentially the same stuff in a styptic pen, used to stop a razor cut from bleeding; apparently it's also great to have on hand for people with leukemia), but as a deodorant if you just rub the block under each pit after you shower and you let it air-dry, you're basically set for 18 hours. It won't stop you from sweating at all, but you won't smell bad.
